h: A castle on an island and a house with a view
p: Threave has a trick up its sleeve that a lot of visitors miss: there's a proper medieval castle on the same stretch of the River Dee. Threave Castle is a great tower house built by the Black Douglases, one of the most powerful families in medieval Scotland. It stands on an island in the river and, in the visitor season, you reach it by a short boat crossing. It's looked after by Historic Environment Scotland rather than the National Trust for Scotland, so check its arrangements separately, but pairing the two makes for a cracking day.

Back at the garden, Threave House is worth a look too. It's a Victorian house in the Scottish Baronial style, all turrets and gables, and its interiors have been restored to show how the family lived in the 1930s. Tours run at certain times of year, so check before you go if you've got your heart set on going inside.

Who'll enjoy it most? Keen gardeners, obviously, but also anyone who likes their days out slow and green. With the borders, the wider estate and the river all in play, give yourself at least half a day.

To round things off, the artists' town of Kirkcudbright is a short drive away, with its colourful streets, harbour and long links to painters. Galloway Forest Park is within easy reach too, famous for its dark skies, if you're staying over and fancy a bit of night-time stargazing.
